## Context / Problem
Plan review LLM calls run at the flat DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS (16000, src/rebar/llm/config.py:269) with no output-budget raise anywhere in the plan-review call sites. A structured response that exceeds the ceiling raises UnretryableOutputError (src/rebar/llm/structured.py; runner.py:628-651 degrades to INDETERMINATE) — observed live on epic a492's container review: one bin over 17 children failed after 333s, and the S7-landed exhaustiveness directive (enumerate every independent defect in one run) deliberately increases per-call finding output, widening this exposure. Truncation here has only bad outcomes: a full-cost re-review or silent loss of critical findings. The completion verifier was remediated for the same family by RAISING the output token budget (completion_recovery.py raises max_tokens, :207/:222); plan review needs the comparable remediation. Operator goal: allow effectively unlimited output tokens for plan-review calls — output is naturally bounded by the model's actual findings, and unspent max_tokens costs nothing.

## Approach
Operator scope extension: the remediation covers ALL review workflows and ALL their LLM passes — plan review (Pass-1 chunks/AGENT/container/ISF/prerequisite, Pass-2 verify + novelty + completion sub-calls, Pass-4 coach, xchecks), the four-pass code review (base finder, Round-A/Round-B overlays, Pass-2 verify, Pass-4 coach — which the Gerrit review-bot inherits), the completion verifier's PRIMARY call (its recovery path already raises; the main call must get the same model-max floor), and review_ticket. scan_spec and the overlap judge are out of scope (not review gates; their outputs are small and schema-bounded). Raise every covered call's output budget to the RESOLVED MODEL'S MAXIMUM output capacity (the API requires a finite max_tokens, so model-max IS the unlimited setting). Mechanism: the runner already lets a request raise the config floor (runner.effective_max_tokens — a request may only raise, and req.output_token_limit still clamps down where bounded recovery needs it). Add a per-model max-output lookup — check first whether the just-landed ModelProfile capabilities seam (change 1014, f184: read capabilities from ModelProfile) exposes max output tokens and use it; otherwise a small table beside sizing.largest_window_tokens with a conservative fallback to the current default for unknown models. Apply it at the plan-review request builders: Pass-1 finder chunks and AGENT criteria, container bins, ISF finder/summarizer, prerequisite finder, and the verify/coach workflow steps (whichever do not already scale via output_tokens_per_item — the verify agentic arm's existing per-item scaling and 64000 ceiling may be replaced by or reconciled with model-max; state the final rule uniformly). Bounded-recovery paths that intentionally clamp via output_token_limit are untouched. Verify timeout interaction: larger max_tokens must not trip request timeouts (cfg.timeout_s; the SDK's streaming requirement for long requests is handled at the transport — confirm by reading anthropic_model.py). Alternative rejected: per-bin child-count scaling (this ticket's earlier draft) — still an arbitrary ceiling; any finite budget below model-max re-creates the truncation class the operator ruled out.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py (request builders), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py (or the ModelProfile seam: model max-output lookup, shared by all workflows), src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml (step budgets reconciled to the one model-max rule), src/rebar/llm/completion.py (primary verifier call floor), src/rebar/llm/operations.py (review_ticket), code-review step builders under src/rebar/llm/code_review/ as needed, tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py (new, covering every workflow's request fields), tests updated where they pin request max_tokens.

## Testing
Unit with a recording FakeRunner: every plan-review request carries max_tokens equal to the resolved model's max output (per the lookup) and never below DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS; unknown model falls back to the default; output_token_limit clamps still apply where set; the verify arm's budget follows the stated final rule; existing plan-review workflow tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every LLM request in the plan-review, code-review, and completion-verification workflows plus review_ticket carries the resolved model's maximum output budget, floor-raised through the existing runner contract (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py` asserting request fields per workflow and per pass, including code-review overlays and the completion verifier's primary call).
- [ ] Unknown/unmapped models fall back to the current default without error (checked: unit test).
- [ ] Bounded-recovery output_token_limit clamps are unaffected (checked: existing recovery tests pass).
- [ ] A synthetic oversized-findings container fixture that previously raised UnretryableOutputError at 16000 completes under the raised budget (checked: unit test with a FakeRunner that enforces the request ceiling).

## 2026-08-08 duplicate consolidation

Duplicate reports: `4e6f-1a2d-482c-435e` and `b54e-9a31-30ff-486b`.

Fresh resolution experiment on current `origin/main`: the complete review-output-budget suite passed `23` tests. It verifies every bespoke plan-review request builder, workflow verify/coach call, completion verification, code review, and review-ticket path uses the resolved model's maximum output budget; its oversized simulated container review exceeds the old default cap and completes. The reported fixed-cap truncation mechanism is therefore absent from the current paths.
